title: Rewire: Advancing CGRA Mapping Through a Consolidated Routing Paradigm
problem: Existing CGRA compilers map dataflow graph nodes individually, neglecting inter-node dependencies; this leads to suboptimal placement that misses opportunities to exploit shared routing and structural locality.
motivation: Coarse-grained reconfigurable arrays balance performance and efficiency, but poor compiler mappings leave substantial performance and compilation time improvements unrealized.
method: Generates shareable routing information via propagation across multiple nodes, intersects routing sets to produce individual placement candidates, utilizes data dependencies as constraints to jointly place multiple nodes in one shot rather than individually.
key_novelty: Consolidated multi-node mapping paradigm that generates shareable routing information and uses data dependencies as placement constraints to place multiple nodes together.
contributions: Shareable routing information generation via propagation across nodes
Data-dependency-constrained joint placement of multiple DFG nodes
13.5× compilation time reduction; 1.3× improvement and 4.7× speedup on second mapper

metrics.speedup: 2.1× performance; 13.5× compilation time reduction (vs. first mapper); 1.3× and 4.7× on second mapper

limitations: Limited to loop kernels in dataflow form; irregular and nested loop support not discussed; scalability to very large DFGs not validated.
primary_theme: Multi-node CGRA mapping with shared routing and dependency-constrained placement
